themes_detail.label: Street Conditions Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints exploded to 127 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 17.8 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 616% spike (z-score: 18.55)—suggesting sudden widespread pavement deterioration, potholes, or surface damage across Jackson Heights/Elmhurst/Corona.
evidence: 127 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 17.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (616% increase)
Z-score of 18.55 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Aligns with repeated CB budget requests for street repairs and new street lights suggesting chronic infrastructure neglect
reporting_angles: Ground canvass: photograph worst-affected blocks; interview residents about transit delays, vehicle damage, pedestrian hazards
City accountability: obtain DOT incident reports, maintenance schedules, and budget allocation data for this district vs. others

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1500% surge (z-score: 8.66)—indicating a sudden coordinated campaign or enforcement gap affecting sidewalks and storefronts.
evidence: 4 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1500% spike)
Suggests either sudden increase in illegal advertising or enforcement action by city
reporting_angles: What changed this week? Contact NYPD and Department of Sanitation for removal logs and enforcement updates
Interview business owners and residents on streets with highest posting concentration about visibility and quality-of-life impact

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Neglect
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK from 0.6 weekly average—an 860% spike (z-score: 6.27)—indicating residents perceive a sudden collapse in sanitation services.
evidence: 6 street sweeping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (860% increase)
Converges with Illegal Posting spike, suggesting broader sanitation infrastructure issue THIS WEEK
reporting_angles: Obtain Sanitation Department schedules: are routes being skipped, vehicles broken down, or staff shortages affecting this district?
Visual survey: compare block-by-block cleanliness to other NYC districts; interview residents on specific locations

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Acceleration
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped to 16 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 3.0 per week—a 433% spike (z-score: 8.67)—suggesting either new breeding grounds or weakened pest control response in the district.
evidence: 16 rodent complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.0 weekly baseline (433% increase)
Long-standing CB budget requests for sanitation and health services suggest chronic underfunding may be breaking down
reporting_angles: Health angle: interview residents and businesses in affected blocks; contact NYC Health Department on disease risk (leptospirosis, hantavirus)
Root cause: has trash collection frequency dropped, have buildings delayed required pest treatment, or are there new waste aggregation points (food vendors, construction sites)?

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints spiked to 13 LAST WEEK from 1.8 weekly average—a 643% increase (z-score: 6.07)—suggesting either weather damage, vandalism, or disease affecting the canopy.
evidence: 13 damaged tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly baseline (643% spike)
Repeated CB requests for park maintenance and safety suggest deferred forestry care
reporting_angles: Investigate trigger: recent high winds, disease outbreak (spotted lanternfly, oak wilt), or vandalism?
Parks Department follow-up: what is response time for tree removal requests in this district?
